text:
marta: hi team — first morning! i want one dev setup for python/node/go/rust on an M1 Air. i'm leaning toward asdf for runtimes but also curious about using Nix for reproducible shells. hit a wall building psycopg2 (gcc/openssl/sqlite issues). any pragmatic path?

devex: welcome marta! :wave: pragmatic patterns we see: 1) asdf on the host for quick iteration, 2) Nix for reproducible CI/devcontainers, or 3) host asdf + nix-shell when you need hermetic build deps. for psycopg2 on Apple Silicon you often need brew sqlite/openssl and the right flags.

archie: fwiw i keep asdf as primary. on M1 i have Homebrew in /opt/homebrew. psycopg2 fix i use: 
```bash
brew install openssl@1.1 libpq sqlite pkg-config
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib -L/opt/homebrew/opt/libpq/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include -I/opt/homebrew/opt/libpq/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib/pkgconfig:/opt/homebrew/opt/libpq/lib/pkgconfig"
# then asdf install python <version>
```
if you also have x86 brew remnants, point the flags to the prefix returned by `brew --prefix openssl@1.1` to be safe.

ryan: another gotcha: some native libs still require x86 builds. if you must use x86 wheels, install Rosetta and an x86 Homebrew under /usr/local and then build under `arch -x86_64` shell. That's annoying but a fallback.

marta: thanks. how do people manage dotfiles here? i'm a fish + starship person.

devex: fish is fine. pattern: keep a repo `~/dotfiles` and symlink (`chezmoi` or plain symlinks). add machine-local files for secrets: `~/.tool-versions-local` and a `~/.env.local` ignored by git. example fish init snippet: 
```fish
# ~/.config/fish/config.fish
set -x PATH $HOME/.asdf/bin $PATH
status --is-interactive; and source (asdf init - | psub)
starship init fish | source
```
use direnv with a fish hook so project envs load automatically.

archie: .tool-versions policy: commit per-repo .tool-versions. keep personal pins in `~/.tool-versions-local` and add it to your dotfiles but don't check it in. asdf plugins i add first: python, nodejs, golang, rust. nodejs plugin needs gpg (brew install gpg) to verify releases.

marta: where do i put REDWOOD_API_KEY and staging creds?

devex: request access to our 1Password vault "Redwood - Developer Secrets". we prefer direnv + op CLI to inject secrets per project. example .envrc (keep it gitignored): 
```bash
export REDWOOD_ENV=development
export REDWOOD_REGION=us-east-1
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="$(op item get \"redwood/staging-api-key\" --fields label=secret)"
```
then `direnv allow` in the repo. don't commit secrets.

ryan: quick tip for long CPython builds: enable `PYTHON_CONFIGURE_OPTS="--enable-optimizations"` if you want optimized builds but be prepared for longer compile time. otherwise use a devcontainer with prebuilt Python image to skip rebuilding.

marta: Nix — worth learning now or defer?

devex: if you care about exact reproducibility and sharing dev shells across the team, learn Nix gradually. most folks start with asdf on host and add a simple `shell.nix` or `devcontainer` for critical repos. infra team can help if you want a Nix-based image.

onboarding-bot: reminder: new hires should request 1Password access and join #devex pairing hours (Wednesdays).

marta: great, i fixed psycopg2 after pointing PKG_CONFIG_PATH at brew prefixes. installing node next. thanks all :raised_hands:
